tool_input.body:
## Summary

`biff enable` (run twice today, once explicitly by the operator) regenerates `.github/workflows/biff-notify.yml` from biff's bundled template even when the repo is already enabled. The regenerated file rolled `astral-sh/setup-uv` back from the v10.3.0 SHA that landed via Dependabot in #275 to v9.0.0, and dropped the comment explaining why the `punt-biff` pin matters.

This commit keeps the one correct change from the regeneration, `punt-biff` 1.16.0 → 1.19.0 (the current release, resolved and run via `uvx`), and restores everything else: the v10.3.0 SHA and the comment. Net diff is one line.

## Why

The `biff-notify` job runs only on a `workflow_run` failure, so this repo's own CI never exercises it; a silent rollback would surface as notifications routing to the wrong relay. The regeneration defect itself is biff's, tracked as `biff-4pcl` (P2): `enable` should be a no-op on an existing workflow, and the template's pin should track Dependabot.

## Verification

docs/CI-only change, no runnable code touched. The `punt-biff==1.19.0` pin was resolved and executed through `uvx` locally. Same shape as the Dependabot bump in #274/#275 that CI already accepted.

tool_input.content:
---
name: justify-guard-before-fixing-it
description: When a local guard (hook, lint rule, gate) misbehaves, ask first whether it is the mechanism or a convenience redundant with a platform guarantee; if redundant, remove it rather than fix it
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-20 the beadle push-guard hook falsely denied a worktree push.
I filed bead beadle-fc6o and ran three missions, five review rounds, and
seventeen commits hardening it (50 lines to 586) before the operator asked
"why do we need this when GitHub branch protection exists?" The answer was
that it never added protection; it was a convenience on top of the real
guarantee, and no sibling repo had one. The operator's verdict: "we have
wasted time on something that's [REDACTED:profanity]."

**Why:** a failing guard looks like a bug to fix. The prior question is
whether the guard is the enforcement mechanism at all. A local hook that
re-implements a platform rule (branch protection, CI gate, signed-commit
requirement) can only ever be redundant for safety, and a redundant guard
that needs a shell parser to work is net negative.

**How to apply:** before dispatching any fix to a hook, lint rule, or gate,
answer in one line: what does this enforce that nothing upstream already
enforces? If the answer is "nothing, it is faster feedback," size the fix
to that (or remove it) and never let it grow a parser. Also check whether
sibling repos carry the same guard; a guard unique to one repo is a smell.
See [[judge-workers-by-transcript-not-hook-files]] for the monitoring
lesson from the same bead.

---
name: nested_worktree_gosec_artifact
description: golangci-lint's path-anchored G204 exclusion fails from ANY git worktree, not just nested ones; the authoritative make check must run from the main checkout
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`.golangci.yml` excludes G204 with `path: ^(internal/pgp|internal/secret|...)/`.
golangci-lint reports a worktree's files relative to the main checkout, as
`../../internal/pgp/x.go` (or `../../../` from `.claude/worktrees/`), so
the `^internal/` anchor never matches and `make lint-strict` reports six
spurious G204 findings. Confirmed 2026-10-22 from both a nested worktree
(`.claude/worktrees/rm-push-guard`) and a flat one (`.tmp/wt-rm-check`):
same six findings, same `../` prefix. The identical linter from the main
checkout on the same tree reports zero.

**Why:** an earlier version of this note blamed nesting under
`.claude/worktrees/` only, and I wasted a scratch worktree proving the
flat case fails too. The cause is the relative-path report, not the depth.

**How to apply:** `make check` from a worktree is not authoritative for
beadle. To verify a branch, confirm the diff touches no `*.go` and no
`.golangci.yml` (then the six findings are provably the artifact), and run
the real gate from the main checkout: `git checkout <branch>` there,
`make check`, `git checkout main`. A worker's make check in its worktree
will hit this; it is not a reason to fail the mission. The real fix is
in beadle: make the exclusion match on the path suffix or use
`path-except`; file it if it keeps costing time.
